title: Graphiti (Zep)
by: Zep Software; open source. Read from the Graphiti README, its edge schema (graphiti_core/edges.py) and its edge resolution and invalidation code (graphiti_core/utils/maintenance/edge_operations.py), and the getzep/zep README. The paper 'Zep: A Temporal Knowledge Graph Architecture for Agent Memory' (arXiv 2501.13956) was not read: arxiv.org was blocked; only search summaries of its abstract were seen.
summary: A framework for a temporal knowledge graph of entities and facts, built from episodes (the raw data as ingested). Every fact edge has valid_at and invalid_at (when it was true in the world) and expired_at (when the system stopped believing it), and lists the episodes it came from. A new fact that contradicts an old one closes the old one by date instead of deleting it. Zep, the hosted product, is built on it.
ideas: Episodes are the ground truth: every entity and fact names the episodes that produced it.
Two timelines: valid_at and invalid_at say when a fact held in the world; created_at and expired_at say when the system learned and dropped it.
Contradiction resolution is a date rule: a candidate that starts later ends the older fact, which gets invalid_at set to the new fact's valid_at and an expired_at.
A fact arriving with an end date is historical at once: it is stored already expired.
Nothing is deleted on contradiction: you can ask what is true now or what was true at any time.
Entity and edge types can be declared up front as Pydantic models (a prescribed ontology) or learned.
Per the paper's abstract as summarised in search results: Zep scores 94.8% on Deep Memory Retrieval (DMR) against MemGPT's 93.4%, and reports gains on LongMemEval.

took.idea: Every derived doc names the raw record it came from
Keep 'when it held' apart from 'when we wrote it'
A deterministic rule decides which of two conflicting docs holds, not a model's judgement
